comment: One case per rule. 'expect' is what the GATE should do (block=exit 2, allow=exit 0, error=any other exit). 'gap': true marks a case that documents a KNOWN LIMITATION rather than desired behaviour — gap cases are reported but never fail the run, so fixing the limitation does not look like a regression. Deliberate-bypass cases stay gap=true while the gate is a text heuristic: the honest claim is 'stops accidents, not adversaries', and those writes are covered by after-the-fact artifact verification instead (see Rule 2 of the skill). The deliberate case builds its path by concatenation on purpose: a text gate never sees the literal protected path.

cases.name: accidental: direct write to protected file
accidental: shell append to protected file
legit: backup copy (source is protected, target is not)
deliberate: path assembled at runtime (string concat)
cases.note: documented gap of text-based gates — expected to be caught by Rule 2 detection, not here
